Reports indicate that Apple will launch its next-generation Apple Silicon chip, the M6, later this year. Below is everything currently known about it, including why this generation is unprecedented in the Apple Silicon era.

M6 Specifications and Performance

According to a report from *Bloomberg*, the Apple M6 chip will feature several major upgrades compared to the current M5 generation.

First, the M6 chip will adopt an updated memory architecture, offering faster memory bandwidth. The current M5 chip has a memory bandwidth ceiling of 153 GB per second.

The M6 is reported to boost memory bandwidth to 200 GB per second. Most notably, the higher memory bandwidth of the M6 chip will improve on-device AI performance.

The M6 chip will also deliver faster performance across all cores, along with improvements in video encoding and decoding.

*Bloomberg* also reports that the M6 chip will feature a redesigned GPU. The current base-model M5 chip supports up to 10 GPU cores, whereas the M6 is reported to feature up to 12 graphics cores. This will result in smoother gaming experiences, faster video rendering, and improved performance in GPU-accelerated applications.

Why the M6 Will Be Different

However, the M6 chip will differ from all previous Apple Silicon chips in one major way.

Since the M1, Apple has consistently released higher-tier "Pro" and "Max" configurations, and has released two "Ultra" chips across the M1, M2, and M3 generations.

The M6 generation will mark a change. According to Mark Gurman, Apple will only release the base-model M6 processor, and will not release any higher-tier Pro, Max, or Ultra variants.

Apple reportedly believes that the improvements in the M7 will be substantial enough to skip most of the M6 product lineup entirely. The M7 chip is reported to deliver greater upgrades for on-device AI processing, including support for memory bandwidth of up to 240 GB per second.

M6 Release Date and Products

The M6 chip is reported to launch as early as later this year. Apple has been testing an updated model of the base MacBook Pro (which currently features the M5 chip).

Whether the M6 chip will be used in other Apple products remains to be seen. The base-model M7 chip is expected to launch in the first half of 2027, so most products will likely skip the M6 generation entirely.

What are your thoughts on Apple's upcoming M6 chip and its strategic shift? Do you think the company made the right call? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
